newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada building permits fall 4.6 pct in December.
newsitem.headline: Canada building permits fall 4.6 pct in December.

text.p: The value of Canadian building permits issued in December fell 4.6 percent to C$2.14 billion, seasonally adjusted, from November, Statistics Canada said on Tuesday.
Nov Month pct chg Yr pct change
Economists surveyed by Reuters had forecast on average a month-on-month rise of 1.8 percent after a 3.5 percent rise in November.
Statistics Canada said building permits for the housing sector have been on the increase since the second half of 1995, led by permits for single-family housing.
"Single-family permits rose a substantial 18.2 percent (in 1996), followed closely by the multi-family component at 17.5 percent," the agency said.
It said favorable housing prices, low mortgage rates and improved economic conditions had brought consumers back to the housing market.
"The results suggest further growth for the new-home market if mortgage rates and house prices remain relatively stable," Statistics Canada said.
Building permits are an early indicator of future demand for labour and material by construction and contruction-related industries.
According to the Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation, about 95 percent of the residential building permits issued translate into actual housing starts.
